title: CVE-2022-43551: Another HSTS bypass via IDN
excerpt:
## Summary:
I found an issue similar to CVE-2022-42916 again.
Since the phenomenon is the same, I will describe the same as last time.

HSTS checks are bypassed if any character in the IDN convert(Nameprep) to a '.'
for example"。"(UTF-8:E38082).
I think there are other characters that become ".(UTF-8:2E)" as a result of converting with IDN.

This is because the host name before IDN conversion is used when writing to the HSTS cache.

## Steps To Reproduce:
[add details for how we can reproduce the issue]

  1. Start from a state where there is no entry for the access destination host name in the HSTS cache
  2. `curl -v --hsts hsts.txt https://accounts.google%E3%80%82com`
  3. `curl -v --hsts hsts.txt http://accounts.google%E3%80%82com`

Result of 3.
```
C:\test\curl-7.86.0-win64-mingw\bin>curl -v --hsts hsts.txt http://accounts.google%E3%80%82com --head
*   Trying 142.250.206.237:80...
* Connected to accounts.google縲Ｄom (142.250.206.237) port 80 (#0)
> HEAD / HTTP/1.1
> Host: accounts.google.com
> User-Agent: curl/7.86.0
> Accept: */*
>
```

If you execute 3. after executing the below, you will access the site with HTTPS.
`curl -v --hsts hsts.txt https://accounts.google.com`

I use [this](https://curl.se/download/curl-7.86.0.zip) in a Windows environment.

I checked the HSTS cache after executing 2. and found the host name before IDN conversion.
```
# Your HSTS cache. https://curl.se/docs/hsts.html
# This file was generated by libcurl! Edit at your own risk.
.accounts.google。com "20231029 15:57:29"
```

I think the problem is in http.c:line 3727.
data->state.up.hostname is the hostname of the IDN unconverted.
```
    CURLcode check =
      Curl_hsts_parse(data->hsts, data->state.up.hostname,
                      headp + strlen("Strict-Transport-Security:"));
```

## Impact

HSTS bypass.
explain: The evidence does not settle it either way.
summary: HSTS bypass via IDN where a hostname containing a Unicode character that converts to '.' bypasses HSTS checks.

claims.text: HSTS checks are bypassed if any character in the IDN converts to '.'
claims.reasoning: The claim that HSTS checks are bypassed when IDN converts a character to '.' requires seeing both the IDN conversion code and the HSTS lookup code to verify a mismatch. The provided snippets show only the call to Curl_hsts_parse (http.c:3727) and the parse function itself (hsts.c:141-239), but not where data->state.up.hostname is populated or where IDN conversion occurs.

claims.text: The host name before IDN conversion is used when writing to the HSTS cache
claims.reasoning: The report asserts that data->state.up.hostname holds the pre-IDN-conversion hostname. The provided code at http.c:3727 passes this field to Curl_hsts_parse, and hsts.c:214,229,236 shows it is used for both storage and lookup. However, the code that assigns data->state.up.hostname (and whether that happens before or after IDN conversion) is not in the provided snippets.

claims.text: Using a hostname with a Unicode character that converts to '.' in an HTTP request
claims.reasoning: This describes a trigger condition (using a Unicode character that IDN-converts to '.'). Verifying whether such a character reaches the HSTS cache in unconverted form requires the IDN conversion code and the hostname assignment code, which are not provided.

claims.text: Access to the site with HTTPS after bypassing HSTS
claims.reasoning: The impact claim (HTTPS access after bypass) is a behavioral consequence. The provided code does not show the HSTS lookup path used during an HTTP request to determine whether an upgrade to HTTPS would occur.

claims.text: Step 2: curl -v --hsts hsts.txt https://accounts.google%E3%80%82com; Step 3: curl -v --hsts hsts.txt http://accounts.google%E3%80%82com
claims.reasoning: Reproduction steps are user-level instructions. They cannot be verified against the provided source snippets alone; they require a running build and the full hostname-resolution/IDN code paths.

key_reasons: The report cites http.c:3727 (data->state.up.hostname) as the flaw location, but the provided snippets do not show where this field is set relative to IDN conversion.

The IDN conversion (Nameprep) code and the hostname resolution code are not included, so the central claim—that the pre-conversion hostname is stored in the HSTS cache while the post-conversion hostname is used for lookup—cannot be confirmed or refuted from the given context.
The report references a prior CVE (CVE-2022-42916) with a similar pattern, making the claim plausible, but the provided code is insufficient to decide.
missing_info: The code that assigns data->state.up.hostname (likely in lib/url.c or lib/urldata.h area) and the IDN conversion function (likely Curl_idnconvert or similar).
The HSTS lookup path used when processing an HTTP request (to see which hostname form is used for the cache query).
reply: Thank you for the detailed report and reproduction steps. To evaluate this, we need to see where `data->state.up.hostname` is populated and whether that happens before or after IDN conversion. Could you point to the function that sets this field, or provide the relevant url.c/urldata.c snippets? Also, the HSTS lookup path used during an HTTP request (not just the parse-on-HTTPS-response path shown) would clarify whether the same hostname form is used for the cache query.
